newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita to brief media on digital broadcasting.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita to brief media on digital broadcasting.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it would hold a news conference at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) in Osaka regarding digital television broadcasting in Britain.
A Matsushita spokesman said the company would make an announcement regarding its business with British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc, or BSkyB.
On Tuesday, another Matsushita spokesman told Reuters that the Japanese electronics giant would soon make an announcement on its investment plans in the project.

Japanese and British media have reported that Matsushita will form a digital television venture with BSkyB, British Telecommunications Plc and Midland Bank SA to sell set-top box adapters for digital television broadcasting.

On Wednesday, the Financial Times reported that BskyB and BT will each have a 32.5 percent stake in the new company and that Midland Bank will have 20 percent. Matsushita will take the other 15 percent, the newspaper said.

It also said BskyB will place orders for one million digital satellite decoders with four consumer electronics companies, including Matsushita, later on Wednesday in deals worth more than 300 million pounds.
The order is the final confirmation that BskyB intends to push ahead with the launch of 200 channels of digital satellite television in Britain, the newspaper said.

In April, the director of Matsushita's European division, Seinosuke Kuraku, told Reuters that Matsushita was in talks with BSkyB over taking a possible stake in the company. But he declined to comment on further details, saying talks were still going on.
